main_text.p: parvis principijs oriri, pro mœnibus usa est septo ligneo è trabibus contexta. Deinde ante annos plus minus CCCC. L. muro lateritio firmo, cum fossa in morem reliquarum urbium cincta fuit, angustiore etiam tum, quàm jam est, ambitu. Nunc ab eo fere tempore, quo tormentorum æneorum usus percrebuit, maximè verò à Caroli bellatoris ducis Burgundiæ ævo, cum is arma Frisiæ minaretur, vallo terreo cum fossa patentiore ampliatis terminis est circumdata: cujus valli ambitus est, in summa superficie, passuum MM. CC. LXXXVI, & in eo mola, quæ ventis agitantur, XII; duæque præter has extra mœnia in latere septentr. Hac amplificatione mœnium postrema versus ortum, meridiem, occasum accessio urbi facta; solum latus boreum, ab eâ amne urbem egrediente, portaque vicina cum parte lateris ortivi ad portam usque Polonam, loco motum non est: atque ita Botterana quoque porta, & Ebbingana, & Polana sedem suam retinuere; reliquæ, maximè Dominica, Orientalis, Steentillana, sunt promotæ. Ex portis his Polona pyramidibus excelsis ac magnis moles duabus, Orientalis etiam quatuor sed gracilioribus, Dominica quinque similibus magnifica specie longè lateque conspicua, decorem civitati non exiguum addidere. Nunc duæ posteriores quondam contra Carolum Burgundum extructæ, altera à Casparo Roblesio.Rursum de portis,

page.notes: The "4" beside "portis" in the right margin is a small reference mark (section sign) belonging to the margin note; it is not transcribed as text. The word "Roblesio" stands on its own line at the right, but it completes the sentence and is read as the last line of the paragraph, not as a catchword. Some words of the first line ("parvis", "principijs") are at the top edge and slightly unclear; "usa" is read from "vsa". The word "egrediente" contains a Cyrillic-looking letter in the scan's OCR-like form; read as Latin "egrediente". "[?]" not added since the reading is consistent.
